items.note: It answers the question directly: the data fits the price increase driving Pro churn but can't prove it. It backs this with Pro vs. Basic before/after counts, which I checked: Pro 10 of 19 (53%) cancelled in Aug–Sep vs. Basic 2 of 18 (11%).
